recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant safety-page prose for FHIR-19251 unless a future work-group decision changes the checklist guidance; handle any remaining DiagnosticReport or DocumentReference boundary concerns through their own Jira keys.
issue_request: FHIR-19251 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I change request to add a Clinical Safety Checklist item warning that content reasonably representable by more than one FHIR resource must still be findable by clients, using DiagnosticReport and DocumentReference overlap as the motivating example, and to create a supporting wiki page.
initial_application: The Jira comment says the safety page change was made in GH#903a769476. Commit 903a769476 added the cross-resource overlap checklist item to source/safety.html; commit 5755ae16f4 migrated the wiki link to Confluence; commit 76ce9865e6 added source/codesystem/codesystem-safety-entries.xml and included the same cross-resource checklist concept.
additional_context: Current source keeps source/safety.html in the built page hierarchy and links it from documentation and implementation-support pages. source/fhir.ini has an active safety-entries CodeSystem entry. The Confluence page Managing Overlap Between Resources references FHIR-19251 and preserves the intended DiagnosticReport/DocumentReference overlap context. Companion issues FHIR-19249 and FHIR-19250 are the same overlap family but concern resource-specific boundary text under OO, so they were not decided here.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. The current safety page already tells implementers to ensure clients can find information when content might reasonably be exposed using more than one FHIR resource, gives mitigation patterns including cross-resource search or exposing data through each applicable resource, and links to the migrated Confluence discussion. The active safety CodeSystem carries the same checklist item.

related_jiras.note: Companion DiagnosticReport boundary issue from the same Baltimore overlap discussion; not decided here because it is OO resource-boundary work applied separately.
Companion DocumentReference boundary issue from the same Baltimore overlap discussion; not decided here because it is OO resource-boundary work applied separately.
